items.stem: Why are vector graphics preferred for a logo that must appear on a business card and a billboard?

options.text: Vectors scale to any size without losing quality
options.rationale: Correct: vectors are defined mathematically and remain sharp at any scale.

options.text: Vectors always have smaller file sizes than any raster
options.rationale: File size depends on complexity; this is not the scaling reason.

options.text: Vectors cannot be edited after creation
Vectors only work in print, not on screen
options.rationale: Vectors (e.g. SVG) work on screen and in print.

items.stem: You want a brand colour change to update across every object that uses it. What should you use?

options.rationale: Correct: editing a global swatch updates every object referencing it.

options.text: A one-off fill colour per object
options.rationale: One-off colours must each be changed manually.
Raster effects do not manage colour references.
Artboards organise layout, not colour references.

items.stem: Which TWO formats are appropriate for exporting a scalable logo?

options.rationale: Correct: SVG is a scalable vector format ideal for web.
Correct: vector PDF preserves scalability for print.

options.text: A low-resolution JPEG as the master
options.rationale: JPEG is raster and lossy; unsuitable as a scalable master.

options.text: A flattened 72dpi PNG as the only deliverable
options.rationale: A single low-dpi PNG is not scalable for all uses.
